text:
sam_marketing: quick one — we need segmented benchmark numbers for the webinar on Tue (4 days). can eng/runtime run a focused sweep that splits results by workload type and sequence length?
elena_marketing: +1 — marketing needs p50/p90/p99 latency and token throughput per-second for the slide deck. also want KV cache on vs off comparisons.
jordan_runtime: we can do it but need specifics. what models/variants, quantization, and exact prompts? and how urgent is raw logs vs aggregated CSVs?
sam_marketing: thanks. ask: 1) two model variants: base open-llm-like fp16 and 4-bit quantized recommended by runtime team 2) sequences: 64, 256, 1024 3) traffic shapes: single-stream low-concurrency (concurrency=1), interactive concurrency (concurrency=8), bulk batch (concurrency=64 with batching) 4) KV cache on/off for chat-style prefix reuse 5) metrics: token-level p50/p90/p99 latency, end-to-end request latency, throughput (tokens/sec), batch sizes, batch wait times, KV cache hit/miss, memory usage, GPU util 6) deliverables: aggregated CSV per run + raw perf logs + brief notes on methodology and commit/docker tag.
elena_marketing: slide need: a single slide with table + 2 graphs (latency tails by seq len, throughput vs concurrency). need these by EOD Monday.
jordan_runtime: ok that timeline is tight but doable if we scope. can you confirm: do we need sampling deterministic outputs? these are perf-only runs so we should use deterministic gen (temperature=0, max_new_tokens fixed). also are we benchmarking streaming vs non-streaming?
sam_marketing: deterministic is fine. non-streaming baseline + streaming sample for interactive only. keep max_new_tokens=128 for seq=64, 256 for seq=256, 384 for seq=1024 so tokens/sec is meaningful.
vikram_runtime: will schedule runs. suggested run config (I'll paste):
```
# runtime harness args
model_variant: "redwood-candidate" # replace w/ exact model name at run time
commit: "<git-sha>"
docker_tag: "gcr.io/redwood/runtime:2026-03-21-perf"
concurrency: [1, 8, 64]
batch_capacity: 128
batch_timeout_ms: 4
quantization: [fp16, 4bit]
kv_cache: [on, off]
prompt_seed: 42
max_new_tokens: [128, 256, 384]
record_histogram: true
export_s3_prefix: "s3://redwood-perf/marketing/webinar/1876543210/"
```
vikram_runtime: we'll also attach run IDs in the CSV and publish raw logs to that S3 prefix. expect ~6 hours per model variant per concurrency shape on the Dedicated cluster (with autoscale).
sam_marketing: perfect. pls include in the CSV columns: run_id, model_variant, quant, seq_len, concurrency, p50_ms, p90_ms, p99_ms, tokens_per_sec, avg_batch_size, batch_wait_ms, kv_hit_rate, gpu_util_pct, commit, docker_tag.
jordan_runtime: noted. also adding a small smoke step: please run one quick 5-min rerun on the public hosted API (low volume) to sanity-check that numbers are not diverging wildly from Dedicated. we can put that in the notes as "hosted vs dedicated sanity".
elena_marketing: can you also include a tiny reproducible snippet so eng-sdks folks can run the smoke locally?
vikram_runtime: yes — sample curl we will include. draft below:
```
curl -X POST https://runtime-api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  -d '{"model":"redwood-candidate","input":"<benchmark-prompt>","max_new_tokens":128,"stream":false,"sampling":false}'
```
sam_marketing: perfect. one more: please snapshot the exact docker image id and the cluster node types used (GPU model, mem). we need that for the methods footnote.
jordan_runtime: will do. also flagging that quantized runs require mapping to the quant profile used (e.g., q4_0 vs q4_1) — we will include that metadata.
vikram_runtime: timeline: kick off today evening, run overnight, aggregate tomorrow morning. will push CSV + raw logs to S3 with public read link for marketing team. expect initial artifact by 2026-03-22 10:00 UTC.
perf-bot: upload complete -> s3://redwood-perf/marketing/webinar/1876543210/hosted-smoke/manifest.json
sam_marketing: awesome. if you hit a blocker (OOM, perf variability >15% between repeats), please ping @jordan_runtime + @vikram_runtime and cc me. we'll deprioritize some shapes if it's unstable.
elena_marketing: can you add a short note on the method section: "each run is 5 replicates, median reported; same prompt seeds; no caching unless specified" — include that in the delivered README.
jordan_runtime: will include run README with: run_id mapping, replicates=5, warmup_requests=50, sampling disabled, harness args, and commit/docker info.
sam_marketing: thanks team. tagging this as high priority for the webinar. :rocket:
elena_marketing: thanks — looping in growth for potential PR talking points after we review numbers.
vikram_runtime: starting the scheduled runs now, will post updates here if anything changes.
